subject: How to use own terrain data (digital elevation model)

messages.subject: How to use own terrain data (digital elevation model)
parts:
I tried to search in this group and still cant figure it out.
I have a high resolution DEM data of 5m of my study area.
I noticed that the DEM used in the micro_era5 does some interpolations and thus it does not represent my area accuratly.
It is possible to feed the model with my own DEM? If so, how?
Thanks in advance.
Kind Regards,
André Fonseca

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: How to use own terrain data (digital elevation model)
parts:
Hi Andre,

Yes that's the way to do it. There are two DEM inputs, 'dem' and 'dem2', both used by microclima with the 'dem2' being used for mesoclimatic adjustments (e.g. cold air drainage, coastal effects) and you might want to make 'dem2' lower res if you were using those features (to save compute time). Also note that if you're running lots of simulations on the same sites with different parameters but the same DEM and you are obtaining the DEM automatically via the elevatr package, as occurs by default, it pays to pre-download the DEMs and save them, and then input them as an argument to the micro_era5 call, rather than have the function go to the web all the time.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: How to use own terrain data (digital elevation model)
parts:
Yes you can just manually put values in the input arguments for 'slope' and 'aspect' (and the horizon angles) from some database - by default they are NA triggering them to be computed from the DEM using microclima::microclimaforNMR
(do ?microclima::microclimaforNMR for more details).
